record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Random Matrix Theory and the Theory of Integrable Systems. II
record.original_question: For random n×n band matrices H with bandwidth w and independent entries inside the band, is the local eigenvalue statistics regime governed by a sharp transition at bandwidth about sqrt(n), with GUE-type statistics when w is much larger than sqrt(n) and Poisson statistics when w is much smaller than sqrt(n)?

evidence.quote: The long-standing conjecture of V. Fyodorov and A. Mirlin [59] from 1991 is that for iid Hij , |i − j| < w, with w ≫ √n, the local statistics of the eigenvalues of H are GUE, but for w ≪ √n, the behavior is Poisson.

artifact.status_search_result: The Fyodorov–Mirlin conjecture (1991) on the $\sqrt{n}$ localization–delocalization transition for 1D random band matrices remains open in full generality. Substantial partial progress has been made: GUE/sine-kernel statistics have been established for sufficiently large bandwidths (e.g., $w \ge n^{3/4}$ and further improvements by Bourgade, Yang, Yau, Yin and collaborators), and the conjecture has been established at zero energy for special chiral band matrix models (Shapiro, 2024). The Poisson side for $w \ll \sqrt{n}$ is essentially unproven.

status_evidence.title: Chiral Random Band Matrices at Zero Energy
status_evidence.snippet: a special model of random band matrices where, at zero energy, the Fyodorov–Mirlin √N-conjecture can be established
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is established only in a special chiral model at zero energy; the general conjecture remains open.

status_evidence.title: Universality for 1d random band matrices
status_evidence.snippet: progress towards the Fyodorov–Mirlin conjecture; bulk universality for bandwidths above thresholds well larger than √n
status_evidence.claim: GUE bulk universality has been proven only for bandwidths much larger than the conjectured threshold √n.

status_evidence.title: A random matrix model towards the quantum chaos transition conjecture
status_evidence.claim: The transition conjecture is described as still a target of current research.
